correctness.rationale: Adding a fixed coin factorization preserves any collision, so the listed translates are contained in the repeat ideal. If a colliding factorization uses two middle coins, it lies in m+S0. Otherwise the middle counts are in {0,1}. Equal middle counts force the extreme w-counts to differ by a multiple of a/gcd(a,2), and the even and odd thresholds put the degree in B+S0 (in the odd case aw=B+(q+d)u). Unequal counts force 2(z0-z1)≡1 mod a, impossible for even a and forcing one of the thresholds B,C for odd a. Both B and C exceed m under the specified hypotheses. The translate description proves closure and cofiniteness; the base-pair identities yield x+y-m∈S for positive x,y, including the special identity 2B-m=C at a=3. Each nonzero Apéry element mod m is indecomposable by that property; each positive s other than m outside Apéry is decomposable as m+(s-m). Hence e=m. Every nonzero Apéry element h yields h-m pseudo-Frobenius, and the converse follows from translating a pseudo-Frobenius f by m. The case f+m=0 is excluded because -m fails on any nonzero Apéry element (m>1). Independent direct enumeration of triples and additive invariants checked 140 coprime cases and 77600 positive offsets, including d>a examples; this is supplementary to the universal proof.
residual_risks: No conclusion for thresholds greater than two or other generator families.

evidence: Adding the smallest coin gives full membership rays, but the theorem needs the behavior of their sums after subtracting m. Equal-length collisions are generated by the u+w=2v relation (the m translate), whereas B and C account for additional collision degrees. The base-pair proof handles q=1 separately and is not merely substitution p=1 into g_p or n_p.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Known membership makes invariants computable for a fixed pair but does not alone show the uniform extremal equalities. A standard minimal presentation, if supplying these Betti degrees, would cover the ideal decomposition via the presentation links, not automatically the base-sum property or type claim. No priority is claimed for the general collision-ideal mechanism.
